title: docs(setup): note the unsigned-binary warning on Windows
body:
## Summary

Adds a short note to the Windows section of `docs/setup.md` and `docs/setup.ja.md` about the security warning Windows shows for the unsigned release binary.

Relates to #87.

## Measured facts (Windows 11 Pro, build 10.0.26200)

- The released `wgft-windows-amd64.exe` (v0.6.0) is not code-signed. `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` reports `Status: NotSigned`, with no `SignerCertificate`.
- Downloading the binary from the GitHub Releases page in a real browser and double-clicking it in Explorer triggers Microsoft Defender SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC" dialog ("Windows によって PC が保護されました"), which blocks the app from starting until you select "More info" and then "Run anyway". The downloaded file's sha256 matched the published hash (`a11033e2854aa6cfb460987a32117f3c028ebc4c2be3aad940c6150cf7173db0`).
- Once approved, Windows removes the file's Mark-of-the-Web (`Zone.Identifier` stream), so the SmartScreen warning does not reappear on later starts of the same file.
- Running the same binary the way this guide actually instructs -- from PowerShell as `.\wgft.exe agent run` -- raises no warning at all, because PowerShell launches a native executable via `CreateProcess`, which does not go through the shell's attachment/reputation check that Explorer's `ShellExecute` path does.

An earlier revision of this PR described a different, older "unknown publisher" attachment-manager dialog instead of SmartScreen; that was based on a hand-written Mark-of-the-Web that didn't reproduce what a real browser download produces, and has been corrected in a follow-up commit to reflect the SmartScreen behavior above.

A later commit also scopes the "Run anyway" bypass claim: Windows' "Warn and prevent bypass" SmartScreen policy can remove that option on a managed machine, so the warning may not always be bypassable the way this guide describes.

## Likely conflict with PR #106

This branch is cut from `main` (not from `docs/verify-windows-download`, which is PR #106 and also edits the Windows section, to add sha256-verification steps). Both PRs touch the same paragraphs in `docs/setup.md` / `docs/setup.ja.md`, so whichever merges second will likely hit a textual conflict that needs manual resolution. Flagging this so the merge order is a deliberate choice, not a surprise.

Recommended order: merge #106 first, then rebase this branch on top of it. After #106 lands, the section reads "verify the hash, then run it," which is the right order for the reader, and rebasing here avoids resolving the conflict on the wrong side.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/check-ascii-punct.sh` passes
- [x] `go run ./scripts/check-japanese/` passes
- [x] `gofmt -l .` is empty (change is docs-only, not expected to affect it)
- Docs-only change; the Go test suite (`go test ./...`) was not run since nothing it covers changed.
